plan.curriculum: English 2.0, Level 5: VC2E5LY02 delivering spoken texts to an audience using features of voice and body; VC2E5LY01 interaction skills when giving and receiving feedback
plan.shape: watch, name, perform: a good and a weak speaker are compared, body language is named, then trios perform speech karaoke cards and give each other feedback
plan.criticalFeature: your body must say the same thing as your words: stance, eyes, hands and face all carry the message
decisionPoints: the choice check: the most confident speaker
the exit board: two fixes for a new speaker
plan.anchor: Claim it. Prove it. Sell it. Say it. Today: say it with your whole body.
plan.catchUp: Missed earlier sessions? Body language is taught from scratch today; perform a karaoke card instead of your own lines.

studentTools: Speech Karaoke Cards (one set per trio, cut before the session)

Point to A, B or C
boardSetup: Stand tall: feet planted, shoulders back, hands still or purposeful, lighthouse eyes (left, middle, right), face matches the words
Trios: speaker, eyes coach, body coach

resources.label: Speech Karaoke Cards
resources.description: Performance activity: six short original speeches to perform in trios with lighthouse eyes and one gesture. One set per trio.
resources.title: Speech Karaoke Cards
resources.subtitle: Perform your card. Use lighthouse eyes, one gesture and one big pause.

cards.text: Friends, our oval is a swamp every winter. Our boots sink. Our games are cancelled. Fix the drains, and give us back our sport!
Every lunch, three bins overflow. Three bins! For six hundred kids! We don't need speeches. We need bins.
I'm only eleven. But I know this: shade saves skin. Plant trees now, and we'll thank you every summer.
Picture a library at lunch. Quiet. Cool. Full of stories. Now picture it locked. Open the doors. Please.
One bottle. One turtle. One choice. Bring your own bottle, and save one more life.
They say kids can't change the world. Watch us. Starting today, our school goes plastic-free.

slides.notes: Open the session. One line: before your audience hears a word, they see you. Today we make that count.

Print and cut one set of Speech Karaoke Cards per trio. Print the Worksheet for everyone, the Extension for early finishers and the Supported Worksheet for those who need it. Clear space for trios to perform.

slides.learningIntention: We are learning to use body language and eye contact to support our message.
successCriteria: I can name body language that helps or hurts a speech.
I can make my body match my words when I speak.
I can give a speaker useful feedback on body language.

beats: POINT to the learning intention.
SAY: Your audience reads your body before your words. Let's make it say the right thing.
SAY: Read the I can lines with me. Everyone, together, on three.
SAY: The first one is where we all start.
The second one is today's main goal.
notes.prep: SC1 is reachable for all; SC2 is the core and the exit evidence; SC3 is the stretch.

slides.title: Guess the feeling
lines: I'll say the same line twice with different body language.

notes.answer: open - the confident version is more believable
beats: SAY: Watch my body, not just my words.
SAY We need your help: slumped, eyes down. Then: tall, eyes up, open hands.
ASK: Which time did you believe me? First or second?
5 sec. Cue: Fingers at your chest, 1 or 2... show me.
EXPECT: 2
ASK: What did my body do differently?
15 sec. Turn and tell, partner A first.
EXPECT: stood tall, looked at us, used hands
SAY: Same words. Your body changed the message. Today we learn to control it.
trap: Fix: say this time the voice was the same; what changed?
notes.prep: Act both versions clearly; it is the hook. 3 minutes.

slides.meaning: Looking at your audience so they feel you are talking to them.

notes.answer: looking at your audience so they feel you are talking to them
beats: POINT to the word. SAY: Eye contact. Say it with me. Eye contact.
SAY: Looking at your audience so they feel you are talking to them.
SAY: Lighthouse eyes: left, middle, right.
ASK: Try lighthouse eyes on your partner's group for one sentence.
10 sec. Turn and tell, partner B first.
EXPECT: eyes sweep left, middle, right
trap: staring at one person the whole time.
Fix: say a lighthouse sweeps; give every part of the room a turn.

notes.answer: feet planted, lighthouse eyes, still or purposeful hands, a matching face
beats: POINT to Feet.
SAY: Plant your feet. If you sway, they watch the sway, not your message.
POINT to Eyes.
SAY: Lighthouse eyes. Left, middle, right. Everyone feels spoken to.
POINT to Face.
SAY: If your words are serious, so is your face. Body and words must agree.
ASK: Stand, plant your feet, and say I can do this with lighthouse eyes.
5 sec. Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
EXPECT: the whole class standing tall
trap: Fix: say one gesture, on one key line. Hands rest the rest of the time.
notes.stretch: Plan where in your speech one gesture will go.
notes.prep: The model. Critical feature: your body must say what your words say.

slides.title: Helps or hurts?
slides.pivot: picture yourself in the audience: are you watching the message or the movement?
slides.followUp: cold call one student: what would you do instead?

items.text: Hands in pockets the whole time
A pause and a look at the audience before the last line
Reading every word from the page
Open hands on Together, we can
items.answer: 1 - helps: the body matches the words

items.text: One step forward for the call to action
items.answer: 1 - helps: it feels urgent and direct

say: One finger helps. Two fingers hurts.
trap: Fix: ask does it match the words? Student re-votes.
notes.stretch: Give a fix for each one that hurts.

options.text: Reads every word with eyes on the page.
Stands still, looks up, pauses, then speaks.
Rocks on heels and laughs between lines.
options.misconception: nerves showing; the body distracts from the words

notes.answer: B - still, eyes up, a pause before speaking
beats: SAY: Three speakers, same speech. Who looks like they believe it?
ASK: Which speaker looks most confident?
10 sec. Cue: voices off, everyone points to A, B or C.
EXPECT: pointing to B
SCAN the room, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, cold call: what would help speaker C?
Less -> act out all three, re-ask.
REVEAL after pointing is scanned.
SAY: B. Still and looking up. The pause says: I'm in charge.
trap: pointing to A because they get every word right.
Fix: ask how does the audience feel when you never look at them?
notes.prep: Decision point before trios perform. Under 80% means a teacher demo of A and B first.

slides.title: Speech karaoke
lines: Trios: speaker, eyes coach, body coach.
Speaker performs a card. Coaches give one glow, one grow.
Swap roles until everyone has performed.

notes.answer: open - every student performs once and coaches twice
beats: SAY: Pick a card. You get thirty seconds to read it twice, then perform.
Lighthouse eyes, one gesture, one big pause.
TIME 4 minutes per speaker, 12 minutes total.
CIRCULATE. Coach the coaches: name one body part in every note.
ASK: Thumbs: how did your performance feel?
5 sec. Cue: Thumbs only, voices off. Show me... now.
EXPECT: mostly up or sideways
ASK: Coaches, tell your speaker one glow and one grow.
20 sec. Turn and tell, eyes coach first.
EXPECT: Your pause was great; look at the left side too
trap: Fix: model: Your eyes were on the floor during the story; lift them.
notes.stretch: Perform your card twice: once calm, once urgent.
notes.help: Perform the shortest card, holding it at chest height.
notes.prep: Fun performance activity with cards; every student speaks. 14 minutes. SC2 and SC3.

slides.title: Plan your body language
slides.task: Work through your Worksheet. Finish by planning your body language for Speech Day, then try it with your own lines.
slides.frame: I will stand ___, look ___, and ___ on ___.

notes.answer: a body language plan: stance, eyes, one gesture, matching face
beats: POINT to the task.
SAY: Plan it, then try it on your own lines from Session 2.
SAY: Read the task, complete each part, check your work.
Finished? Extension next. Everyone, together, on three.
CIRCULATE. Ask: where will you look? Which line gets your gesture?
ASK: Perform one line with your plan for your partner.
30 sec each. Turn and tell, partner A first.
EXPECT: planted feet, eyes up, one gesture
trap: a plan with a gesture on every line.
Fix: student picks the single most important line for the gesture.
notes.stretch: Extension: plan movement across your speech, then coach a partner.
notes.help: Supported Worksheet: picture-clue choices, a first gesture done, a short plan.
notes.prep: Independent planning, then a quick paired try. SC2.

slides.title: Show what you know
questions: A speaker says Our playground needs shade, now! while staring at her notes and twisting her feet.

notes.answer: eyes up to the audience; feet planted; a gesture on now
beats: SAY: A new speaker. Coach her in two fixes.
ASK: Write two body language fixes.
45 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: look up; plant feet; matching face; a gesture
RECORD who gives voice fixes only. Speech Day rehearsal group.
trap: Fix: none now, record the name.
notes.prep: Exit evidence for SC2 on a new speaker. One board per student.

notes.answer: open - lighthouse eyes in the mirror
